How to build a real SaaS with AI, from zero How to build a real SaaS with AI, from zero: a website that sells it, logins, a database, monthly payments and photos, all built by talking to Claude Code. I never wrote a line of code. The example: MenuTap, a $9/month QR menu app for cafés. 1. The tool: Claude Code inside VS Code (the extension), a paid Claude plan, an empty folder. 2. The first draft looked like every AI site, so: the free frontend-design plugin + "make it look premium" + 6 AI photos. 4. The database: Supabase, running on your own computer first. Publishable key in the browser, secret key only on the server. 5. The rule: anyone can read a published menu, only the owner can edit it. Put it in the database, then make the AI prove it with a second owner. It tried 24 ways. All failed. 6. Customer side: the public menu + a QR code that holds a permanent link. 7. Payments: a Stripe sandbox, $9/month, a webhook unlocks the account. 4242 unlocks, the decline card stays locked, fake "she paid" messages get refused. 8. Photos, then a security review before launch: nothing critical, 13 real problems, 11 fixed. 9. Online: GitHub (private), Vercel (Pro, because taking payments is commercial use), the online Supabase project, your domain. The 3 things that break on launch day: login emails (use Resend), login links pointing to localhost (set the site URL), and live Stripe keys + a new webhook.
